# Rung H (rung-ast-hashes): the record lines

## FACTS

- **The syntax tree's hashes do not depend on the JVM's identity hashes; one checker site still does.**
  - Every generated node's hash starts from the hash of its class's name. makeAST's post-processing of ASTGen's output and the in-repo generators write it (`build.xml:679-697`).
  - A field whose type holds an Option is hashed by `NodeHash.of` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeHash.java`), since the PLT Option classes hash by identity hashes.
  - So hash maps and sets of nodes iterate in one order whatever code asked for an identity hash before, and so do the apis that `StaticChecker.checkApis` takes in turn.
  - Two kinds of node still hash by an identity hash: `_InferenceVarType`, `_InferenceVarOp` and `_InferenceVarInt`, whose id is a bare `Object` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeFactory.java:1166-1184`), and walk's `_WrappedFValue`, which hashes its `FValue` (`interpreter/evaluator/_WrappedFValue.java:170-177`). No output of the count stage moves through the first (`compile-ladder/rung-ast-hashes/REPORT.md`, section 4.4); the second is walk's own (row 430).
  - The checker's output still moves at row 488's `:130`, through NEW-H-1.
  - The entry replaces F-232, which the change makes false.
  - Test: `NodeHashJUTest.testHashesDoNotDependOnIdentityHashes`; for the site that still moves, `XXXOmittedReturnTypeFromApi.test`.
  - Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-ast-hashes/REPORT.md`, sections 4.2 to 4.4.
- F-53's sentence "An edit can move 2 to 4 errors that it does not touch (row 488; F-232)" holds now only through NEW-H-1. Read: "An edit can move errors that it does not touch where a component's function leaves out its return type beside a same-named api declaration (row 488; NEW-H-1)". This rung's edit, which touches no library line, moved one such error, `:130`, in the distance stage (`compile-ladder/rung-ast-hashes/REPORT.md`, section 7).

## Ledger notes

- **Row 488.** Its notes hold 686 of their 700 characters, so this text is for the coordinator: "Climb batch 16 rung H fixed the nodes' hashes; the H runs then move only `:130` (absent at N = 0, present at 1 and 1000). Mechanism: NEW-H-1. `ApiTypeExtractor` gives `BIG LEXICO(g)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:129-130`) the nullary declaration's `BigReduction` return type when that comes first in `DeclaredFunction` identity-hash order (`compile-ladder/rung-ast-hashes/REPORT.md` 4.3)."
- **Row 430** (at its limit; for the coordinator): "Climb batch 16 rung H fixed the syntax tree's hashes. Walk's orders here come from `FType`'s counter and `FunctionClosure`'s identity hash, which it left; testSystem's 621 verdicts are unchanged."
- **Row 730** (at its limit; for the coordinator): "Climb batch 16 rung H regenerated the nodes twice: `FortressAst.scala` is byte for byte the same and `WalkerJUTest` passes 4/4."
- **Row 577:** "Climb batch 16 rung H moved no library line; its distance sites, read by row: `:130` gone, `:1463`'s union reversed."

## New rows

Section "3. Traits, objects and components":

| NEW-H-1 | the compiled checker gives a component's function that leaves out its return type the return type of the exported api's first declaration of its name, in identity-hash order, not of the declaration of its own parameter type, so one overload's body is checked against another's (`ApiTypeExtractor`) | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (checker) | `basic/components/type-inference.tex`, "Type Inference for Components" | `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXOmittedReturnTypeFromApi.test` | climb batch 16 rung H | `isExported` returns the first `SDeclaredFunction` of `functions.matchFirst(name)` and compares no parameters (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ApiTypeExtractor.scala:116-122` at 528438ac5); the relation is an `IndexedRelation` (`IndexBuilder.scala:158-159`) of `DeclaredFunction`s, which declare no `hashCode` (`compiler/index/DeclaredFunction.java:25`), so the pick moves with the identity-hash sequence. Row 488's `:130` is this case: `BIG LEXICO(g)` takes `BIG LEXICO()`'s `BigReduction` when that comes first. Compiled path only: walk checks no types. Workaround: write the return type. |

44:- For a refusal at load, put `Name.test` beside `tests/Name.fss`, with `load_exception_contains=<message>`. A plain test is green if walk refuses the program at load as named. A failure while the top-level variables are initialised counts as a refusal. An `XXX` test with such a `.test` file is green if the program loads and runs clean.
70:## How `XXX` works
72:- Under walk, an `XXX` test is `tests/XXXName.fss`, whose component is `XXXName`. With no `.test` file, it is green when it fails as a plain test would.
73:- In the compiled test folders, the `XXX` prefix of a `.test` file's name applies to every command that the file drives: each must fail. So a defect at run time, whose link succeeds, needs two `.test` files ("Writing an `XXX` test").
75:- The harness reports any link or compile exception of a component whose name contains `XXX` as expected, whatever the `.test` file's name. Only an unmet key of that command makes it red.
76:- An `XXX` compile test with a `compile_err_contains` key, whose program compiles, reports "Saw wrong failure", which is red.
77:- A green `XXX` test prints `Saw expected failure` or `OK Saw expected exception`.
83:1. Your change repairs it: an assertion in your plain gated test. It needs no `XXX` stage.
84:2. It is deferred, and the specification settles it: a gated `XXX` test that asserts the specification's answer. Write it in the change that measured the defect, even if a later change will repair it. A deferred defect of a program that the checker accepts and that then fails the JVM's verification (`VerifyError`), linkage or a range check at run time is one of these.
101:## Writing an `XXX` test
103:In a compiled test folder, name the component `XXXName`, in its file `XXXName.fss` and in its `component` line.
105:- For a refusal at compile time, write one `XXX` compile test, with `compile` and `compile_err_contains=<the refusal's message>`.
106:- For a code-generator wall (`compiler.md`, "What the compiled path cannot compile yet"), write `XXXName.test` with `tests=XXXName`, `compile` and `compile_exception_contains=<text of the exception>`.
108:  - `NameLink.test`, a plain name, with `tests=XXXName` and `link`. It is red if the link reports static errors, but green on an exception.
109:  - `XXXName.test`, with `tests=XXXName` and `run`, and no `link`. Its run uses the plain file's link, so run the two files in one call of `junit.sh` or `fortress junit`, the plain one first.
110:  - The program prints `REACHED` in `run()` before the part that fails. The `XXX` file checks it with `run_out_contains=REACHED`, or with `run_out_does_not_contain=REACHED` if the run dies before `run()` prints. Never use `run_out_contains=PASS`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`). Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the
record file and its history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

  PROVENANCE: --from PATH#HEADING (repeatable; PATH from the repository root
  or from explorations/, HEADING held by exactly one heading of it, as doc:
  resolves one), --commit HASH (in HEAD's history), --by WHO, --note WHY.
  Each write needs --from or --note.

  add F|P --section TITLE FILE   a new entry from FILE's one line, numbered
      record.py add F --section 'Landed semantics' new.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The fix' --by coordinator
  set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] entry N rewritten from FILE's line, or moved
      record.py set F-87 f87.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The question' --note 'cut to the form'
  merge N --into M [FILE]        N removed, M rewritten from FILE (or kept),
                                 every pointer to N made a pointer to M
      record.py merge F-90 --into F-87 f87.md --note 'one fact, two entries'
  remove N                       N removed; refused while a pointer to it remains
      record.py remove P-131 --note 'evicted to the coordinator skill, references/briefing.md'
  apply FILE                     many changes from one file, all or none (below)
      record.py apply chunk3.md --by 'consolidation chunk 3'
  check [--base COMMIT]          the store's checks; exit 1 on a failure
      record.py check --base cc9424c2a

An apply file holds, in any order: `## TITLE` or `### TITLE`, the section the
new entries below it go to (an existing entry stands under no heading, or
under its own section's, or the `## ` one that holds it); entry lines as they
should stand, `- F-87 ...`, or `- F-?1 ...` for a new entry, its placeholder
replaced by its number everywhere in the file; `move F-87 to SECTION`;
`remove F-90`; `merge F-91 into F-87`. Each may be followed by one indented
provenance line of its own:
`  from: PATH, "HEADING"; commit: HASH; by: WHO; note: WHY`. Blank lines and
`<!-- -->` comments are ignored. An entry line equal to the entry is skipped.

check fails on: an entry line without its number, or a line under an entry
that continues it; a number on two lines; a number with no `numbered` or
`added` block, or one gone from its file whose last block is not `merged into`
or `removed`; a pointer to no live entry, or quoted words that do not open the
target's title; with --base, an entry at COMMIT that is neither its line now
nor the earlier line of a block in its history (pointer words refreshed by the
tool aside). It reports, without failing: the entries over 600 characters, the
entries without a bold title, and the `--from` paths and the report sections
an entry cites (`PATH`, "HEADING") that do not resolve.

component GenericBoundsMeetWalk
export Executable
(* Two generic declarations over ListI[P], one with P bounded by A and one by B, beside a third whose parameter is bounded by both, are a valid overloading, and a ListI of a type below both runs the third (overloading.tex, section "Declarations with Static Parameters"). *)
trait A end
trait B end
trait C extends { A, B } end
object Ao extends A end
object ListI[\X\] end
sort[\P extends A\](x: ListI[\P\]): String = "A"
sort[\Q extends B\](x: ListI[\Q\]): String = "B"
sort[\R extends { A, B }\](x: ListI[\R\]): String = "A and B"
run(): () = do
    assert(sort(ListI[\C\]), "A and B", "ListI[C] runs the declaration bounded by both A and B (overloading.tex, section \"Declarations with Static Parameters\")")
    assert(sort(ListI[\Ao\]), "A", "ListI[Ao] runs the declaration bounded by A")
    println("PASS")
  end
end

**Finding 1, a correction of the test, settled.** The rung changed the hash line of the three in-repo generators, of the 18 classes of `parser_util/precedence_opexpr/`, and of `useful/Cons.java` and `useful/Empty.java`. Its test printed only classes of ASTGen's own template, so none of those edits had a test that fails without it. The skill settles it: "Write the test before the fix for every edit of source code in the original tree" (`.claude/skills/fortress-repo/SKILL.md:160`), and so does the brief's "Tests, first". The correction, `1038ac9a6`, adds seven lines to `Print`: the hashes of a `TemplateGapExpr`, an `_EllipsesExpr`, an `_SyntaxTransformationExpr`, a `Cons`, an `Empty`, a `Higher` and a `RealExpr`. It leaves out `_WrappedFValue`, whose hash still takes its `FValue`'s identity hash, walk's own (row 430).

content.content:
static type that it does not have: by the declared type of the local variable,
or the declared return type of the top-level or local function, whose value the
reduction or the comprehension is, also as the last expression of a block, where
that type fixes the big operator's result type; otherwise by the join of the run-time types of
the elements that its generator clauses give, which it collects before it
reduces them; and where there is no element, at the bound of each static
parameter, or open where the bound mentions the parameter itself.
So an empty sum that is the value of a function declared \EXP{\mathbb{R}64}
is the \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} zero, and the library's set reductions
\EXP{\bigcup} and \EXP{\bigcap} run on sets of their elements' type; but an
empty reduction that no declared type directs takes the identity of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} whatever the type of the expression, and an empty
comprehension that no declared type directs is built at the bound, a list
comprehension as a \EXP{\TYP{List}\llbracket\TYP{Any}\rrbracket} (row~716 of the
revival's gap ledger); a comprehension that no declared type reaches, such as
the value of a top-level variable, a field, a method or a function expression,
the right-hand side of an assignment, the body of another reduction or an
argument of a call, is
built at the run-time types of its elements, which the declared type of an
enclosing expression may not admit (rows~20, 510 and~717).
A big operator whose declared result is none of the library's
\TYP{BigReduction}, \TYP{Comprehension} and \TYP{BigOperator} it instantiates
through the one of those three that its declared result extends, with that
trait's static arguments.
It gives a function expression that declares no return type the return type
\TYP{BottomType}, so that a type parameter that only its result fixes is
instantiated there (row~587); and it leaves a generic method's static
parameters uninstantiated (row~21).

blockingCode: Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2633-2636 (the Effect of 'Overloading with static parameters'; this is the gather's correction of rung W's sentence after K's hunk). The text reads: 'The interpreter refuses at load two declarations with static parameters whose parameter types, each read over its own instances, are each a subtype of the other, as \VAR{dup}'s are; it loads such a pair and runs one of them where one has static parameters and the other's parameter type is its bound (row~549).' The first clause now spells out its subject as two declarations with static parameters, so 'such a pair' in the second clause names two generic declarations. Read that way, the sentence says walk loads two generic declarations with equal domains where one's parameter type is the other's bound. Walk refuses such a pair: for two own generics, OverloadedFunction.java:764 returns `withdrawn && genericPairValid(...)`, and genericPairValid refuses two domains that each lie inside the other (OverloadedFunction.java:810, `if (gHolding != null && fHolding != null) return false`). Row 549 is a different pair: a generic declaration beside a plain one, `tie[\T extends Wide\](a: T, b: T)` beside `tie(a: Wide, b: Wide)` (fortress-gap-ledger.md, row 549). This breaks check 4: a sentence made false must be corrected to what the code does. Suggested repair: name row 549's pair, e.g. '...; it loads a declaration with static parameters beside a plain one whose parameter type is the first's bound, a pair the same rule refuses, and runs one of them (row~549).'

Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2614-2617 (the same Effect; the gather's text in place of rung W's skeptic's correction). The text reads: '..., except where a pair of their parameter types excluded each other only when both declarations were read at one instantiation, as instances of one generic object do: such a pair it reads on the two declared domains, each over its own instances, by these rules.' The plain reading of 'both declarations were read at one instantiation' is one instantiation shared by both. That reading misses the pairs walk now loads through this exception. GenericBoundsMeetWalk's `sort[\P extends A\]` and `sort[\Q extends B\]` over `ListI` (ProjectFortress/tests/GenericBoundsMeetWalk.fss) and dup's pair have different lists of static parameters. Walk gives each list its own symbolic instantiation (GenericFunctionOrMethod.java:47-66, the partition by name and static parameters; FGenericFunction.java:43-64). Their `ListI[P]` and `ListI[Q]` excluded because two distinct instances of one generic object cannot be extended (FType.java:212-217). At one shared instantiation they would be one type and would not exclude. So, read plainly, the sentence says walk refuses GenericBoundsMeetWalk's set, which it loads (F-238). Rung W's skeptic named this wording as failing (354c002fa: 'read at one instantiation of both ... fails for dup's, sort's and GenericBoundsMeetWalk's pairs'). The gather dropped 'of both' but kept 'both declarations were read at one instantiation' (RECORD.md 'Corrections, after K's hunk', item on :2612-2614). Suggested repair: name walk's own reading, e.g. 'excluded each other only in the interpreter's reading of each declaration at one symbolic instance of its static parameters, shared where the two declare the same ones, as two instances of one generic object then do'. The review made the same correction to F-238's title in 07c83a40a.

It now says 'excluded only in walk's reading of each at one symbolic instantiation', which its body states (FGenericFunction.java:43-64; FType.java:212-217). Commit 07c83a40a.
